answer_text:
Let

\[
a_p=\sum_{k=0}^p (-1)^k \binom pk \frac1{(k+2)(k+4)}.
\]

First simplify \(a_p\). Since

\[
\frac1{(k+2)(k+4)}
=\frac12\left(\frac1{k+2}-\frac1{k+4}\right),
\]

we have

\[
a_p=\frac12\left(\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+2}
-\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+4}\right).
\]

For a positive integer \(m\),

\[
\frac1{k+m}=\int_0^1 x^{k+m-1}\,dx,
\]

so

\[
\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+m}
=\int_0^1 x^{m-1}\sum_{k=0}^p\binom pk(-x)^k\,dx
=\int_0^1 x^{m-1}(1-x)^p\,dx.
\]

This is a beta integral:

\[
\int_0^1 x^{m-1}(1-x)^p\,dx
=B(m,p+1)
=\frac{(m-1)!p!}{(p+m)!}.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+2}
=\frac{1!p!}{(p+2)!}
=\frac1{(p+1)(p+2)},
\]

and

\[
\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+4}
=\frac{3!p!}{(p+4)!}
=\frac6{(p+1)(p+2)(p+3)(p+4)}.
\]

Therefore

\[
a_p
=\frac12\left(
\frac1{(p+1)(p+2)}
-\frac6{(p+1)(p+2)(p+3)(p+4)}
\right).
\]

Simplifying,

\[
a_p
=\frac{p+6}{2(p+2)(p+3)(p+4)}.
\]

Now decompose into partial fractions:

\[
a_p
=\frac12\left(\frac2{p+2}-\frac3{p+3}+\frac1{p+4}\right).
\]

Let \(S_n=a_0+a_1+\cdots+a_n\). Then

\[
S_n=\frac12\sum_{p=0}^n\left(\frac2{p+2}-\frac3{p+3}+\frac1{p+4}\right).
\]

Using harmonic numbers \(H_m=1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1m\),

\[
\sum_{p=0}^n\frac1{p+2}=H_{n+2}-1,
\]

\[
\sum_{p=0}^n\frac1{p+3}=H_{n+3}-\frac32,
\]

\[
\sum_{p=0}^n\frac1{p+4}=H_{n+4}-\frac{11}{6}.
\]

Hence

\[
S_n
=\frac12\left[
2(H_{n+2}-1)-3\left(H_{n+3}-\frac32\right)
+\left(H_{n+4}-\frac{11}{6}\right)
\right].
\]

The constant part is

\[
-2+\frac92-\frac{11}{6}=\frac23.
\]

Also,

\[
2H_{n+2}-3H_{n+3}+H_{n+4}
=-\frac2{n+3}+\frac1{n+4}.
\]

Therefore

\[
S_n=\frac12\left(\frac23-\frac2{n+3}+\frac1{n+4}\right)
=\frac13-\frac1{n+3}+\frac1{2(n+4)}.
\]

Taking \(n\to\infty\),

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}(a_0+a_1+\cdots+a_n)=\frac13.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac13}
\]

27B·v4.method: Partial fraction on 1/((k+2)(k+4)), Beta integral to evaluate the alternating binomial sum exactly, then partial fractions and harmonic-number limit.
